FLASHCARD SET · AGES 2–5 YEARS

Cafeteria food flashcards.

Sixty-two foods, sixty-two things to do with them. Each card names one cafeteria item — the apple, the spaghetti, the milk carton — and prints one activity under its name: point to the apple, count the peas, match the sandwich. Each food has its own short page, a full lesson and a printable twin in the library. Little lunches start with the tray card and grow one food at a time.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Set the real tray

    Put a real plate, cup and napkin on the table, deal three cards, and let the child build a matching lunch — card to table, table to card. Real trays eat the learning.

  2. 02

    Cafeteria queue

    Line the cards up like a serving line: main dish first, sides next, drink last. Walking a toy along the line and choosing one of each is the whole lunch ritual in miniature.

  3. 03

    Count the shelf

    Deal five counting cards — the peas, the carrots, the berries — and count every picture out loud. Food is the friendliest counting material in the house.

  4. 04

    Pack the pretend lunch

    Pick one main dish card, one fruit, one drink and slide them into a paper bag. Unpacking and naming the bag’s lunch is a game that repeats all week.
